      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.

          title: First name

          type: string
          minLength: 1

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized into
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits. Stored and returned in E.164 form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[-0-9 ()+.]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it
            defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date

## Summary

I implemented the household-duplicate rejection rule on `POST /api/owners`: an owner is rejected with **409 Conflict** when another owner already has the same `lastName` **and** `address` (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

Changes, following the existing `DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException` pattern already in the codebase:

- **`openapi.yml`** — added a write-only `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema so the flag is bound onto the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` (unknown JSON fields are otherwise silently dropped) without appearing in owner responses.
- **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException.java`** (new) — runtime exception carrying the offending last name/address.
- **`ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — a handler mapping that exception to a 409 `ProblemDetail` whose `errors` array names `lastName` and `address`.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — added `normalizeHousehold` (trim + collapse internal whitespace + lowercase) and `requireUniqueHousehold`, invoked after the telephone check and skipped when `sharesHousehold` is true. Existing owners' fields are normalized the same way before comparison.

Test results: `Tests run: 20, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — the full suite is green, including the three new `Cp10Tests` (reject same last name + address, allow when address differs, allow when `sharesHousehold` is true).
